items.q: Why custom development instead of a template?
items.a: Templates suit specific cases, such as Shopify for a straightforward store or WordPress for a blog. When a business has its own workflows, local payment methods or roles that do not fit a plugin, the template becomes the limit. A custom build is designed around those rules and stays yours.

items.q: How long does a custom build take?
items.a: Delivery runs {deliveryWeeksMin}–{deliveryWeeksMax} weeks depending on scope and complexity. The estimator gives an indicative range, and your proposal sets the delivery window once the scope is agreed.

items.q: What do you build on?
items.a: Next.js, in a typed codebase, deployed on Vercel or on your own infrastructure. Every language lives in one codebase with right-to-left layout built in.

items.q: Do we own the code?
items.a: Yes. The source code, database schema and documentation are handed over in your repository, and code, designs and accounts pass to you at the final payment. There is no licence fee and no lock-in.

items.q: How is the price set and paid?
items.a: The published range depends on project type and complexity, and the price is fixed in the proposal. Payment is split {paymentStart} to start, {paymentMilestone} at {milestoneTrigger}, and {paymentFinal} before production launch.

items.q: What happens after launch?
items.a: A {warrantyDays}-day warranty covers critical fixes. After that, you choose a maintenance plan, pay for changes as needed, or hand the system to your own team with the documentation it needs.

items.q: Can you maintain a site you did not build?
items.a: Yes. We check its stack and current state first, then recommend the plan that fits it. If the site needs a deeper look before anyone maintains it, the technical audit is the place to start.

items.title: One screen, one job.
items.body: Every page is built around the one action it exists for, mapped from where a visitor arrives to where they decide. Everything else on it either supports that action or leaves.

items.title: Your identity, as a system.
items.body: Colour, type and spacing become rules your team can extend — not a style that drifts the first time someone edits a page.

items.title: Fast is a design decision.
items.body: Every image, font and animation is weighed against load time before it ships. A beautiful screen that loads late is a screen nobody sees.

items.title: Readable by everyone.
items.body: WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and structure, checked in every language — a requirement of the design, not a fix after launch.

fit.description: Interface design starts from what a page or screen has to make someone do. If you know that, or want help deciding it, this is the service.

A dashboard or portal works, but the people using it get lost.
Every language has to read as an equal, not one translated from another.
You want the design handed over as rules your team can extend, not a folder of pictures.

items: You need an existing theme restyled. We design from your requirements, never from a recycled template.

items.q: What does website and interface design include?
items.a: The sitemap and page structure, the key user flows, responsive designs for every screen in scope, and a working design system of colour, type, spacing and components. The designs pass to you with the code at the final payment.

items.q: How much does website design cost?
items.a: Design is part of every website build, which starts from {minimumEngagement} and is fixed in your proposal. Design ordered on its own, without our build, is scoped per project.

items.q: How long does the design phase take?
items.a: Wireframe and design are short, fixed phases of the project process, and their lengths are published on the Process page. Your proposal sets the dates. The largest variable is review time, because each phase waits for your approval.

items.q: How many revision rounds are included?
items.a: {revisionRounds} included revision rounds, written into your proposal before work starts. Revision work beyond them is billed at {revisionRate} an hour, and you approve the figure before that work begins.

items.q: Do you design for right-to-left languages?
items.a: Yes. Right-to-left languages are laid out as their own design, not mirrored after the fact, and every language is checked for contrast and structure against WCAG 2.1 AA.

items.q: Can you redesign an existing website?
items.a: Yes. We start from what the current site has to do and where it falls short, rebuild the structure, then design the screens. If the problem may be technical rather than visual, the technical audit answers that first.
